content.title: About
content.content: Haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) is a cold‑water fish of the cod family found in the North Atlantic. Raw haddock fillets are pale pink to white, have a delicate flavor and a moderately firm texture. It is commonly used in sushi, ceviche and as a base for marinades.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Haddock can grow up to 1 m in length and weigh over 10 kg.
Historically, haddock has been a staple of the British fish‑and‑chips industry.
The flesh is high in protein but low in fat, making it popular in diet‑focused dishes.
Haddock can change the color of its skin to blend with the surrounding water.
In some Arctic communities, haddock is considered a vital source of nutrition during winter months.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Raw haddock provides about 18 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Its low saturated‑fat content makes it suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and B6, which are essential for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains selenium, iodine and phosphorus, important for thyroid health and bone strength.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower than fatty fish, haddock still supplies EPA and DHA, beneficial for brain health.

items.title: Parasite risk
items.content: Raw fish may harbor parasites such as Anisakis. Freezing at –20 °C for at least 7 days is recommended before consumption.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Haddock from polluted waters can accumulate mercury and other toxins; choose reputable sources.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including haddock.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thinly slice raw haddock for sushi, sashimi, or marinate in citrus juice for ceviche. Rinse the fillet well and pat dry before serving. Common accompaniments include soy sauce, grated ginger and sliced green onions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw haddock in an airtight container at 0 °C–2 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C for at least 3 months. Before use, check for a fresh, mild scent; any strong ammonia odor indicates spoilage.
